claims.text: A qualifying high-entropy-alloy solid solution must contain at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 at.% each.
Ta0.34Nb0.33Hf0.08Zr0.14Ti0.11 is a representative superconducting HEA baseline composition.
The baseline Ta0.34Nb0.33Hf0.08Zr0.14Ti0.11 alloy is Nb-Ta-rich and contains relatively little Ti.
The representative baseline belongs to a BCC superconducting HEA class.
The representative baseline has a chemically disordered lattice.
Increasing Ti relative to Nb and Ta while retaining the BCC phase will increase Tc.
Increasing Ti relative to Nb and Ta while retaining the BCC phase will increase Hc2.
Increasing Ti increases the effective electron-phonon coupling of the HEA.
Increasing Ti beneficially alters the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Increasing Ti changes the local bonding environment.
An optimal balance exists between disorder-assisted pairing and disorder-related suppression or scattering.
Strong compositional disorder on a BCC lattice can be associated with superconductivity even when the constituent binary alloys are not superconducting above 2 K.
A single-phase, chemically disordered BCC lattice supports uniform electron transport.
The proposed superconducting enhancement is conditional on retention of a disordered, single-phase BCC structure without deleterious phase segregation.
Excessive Ti may induce phase separation or ordering that prevents the predicted superconducting enhancement.
Previously reported type-A BCC HEA superconductors have Tc values of 4.0-9.2 K and maximum μ0Hc2 close to 12 T.
Keeping synthesis parameters constant ensures that observed superconducting changes derive solely from composition.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes Ti-rich samples that undergo phase separation or structural change, but the falsification rule treats such changes as falsifying the hypothesis rather than as tests outside its stated domain.

The prediction allows enhancement of Tc and/or Hc2, whereas the falsification wording refers to consistent enhancement of Tc and Hc2, making it unclear whether improvement in only one property confirms or falsifies the hypothesis.
